items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: we played a lot with Dennis Budimir

ctx.x: Can you define “adventurous” at that point in the west coast jazz scene?

Ornette Coleman’s first record came out, the second record came out while I was still in high school, and I loved them, I bought them and I loved them. The reason I bought them was they were on Contemporary Records which was my favorite label, and I had already got to meet and, you know as a teenager gotten to meet and play with Art Pepper and I listened to “Shelly Manne and His Men” were on that label and I loved everything on Contemporary Records. I would just get it, and I saw Ornette Coleman on the album with…
Now those guys followed the path into the studios and I’m assuming they made a pretty good living. Did you aspire to that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
